text:
sarah-infra: Heads-up: seeing p95/p99 jump and request timeouts from multiple customers in us-west2-hostpool starting ~03:20 UTC after the kernel RT clock sync kernel-5.15.72 rollout. Customers report 2–3x tail latency on generation endpoints.

alex-sre: Noted. Any correlation with CUDA/driver updates or NVMe firmware?

sarah-infra: We only pushed the host kernel timesync patch last night. No driver/firmware changes. Rolling median latency looks stable, but p95 and p99 spiked. Attaching quick sample: 
```
endpoint: /v1/generate
host: host-uw2-17
window: 03:15-03:40 UTC
median: 110ms -> 120ms
p95: 310ms -> 920ms
p99: 720ms -> 2.1s
errors: 0.8% -> 4.6% (timeouts)
queue_depth_avg: 35 -> 120
```

mike-rt: queue_depth up from 35 to 120 is concerning. Could be blk layer qdepth backpressure after timesync changed timer granularity. @ryan-eng-runtime can you check whether our runtime scheduling changed to prefer co-operative yielding?

ryan-eng-runtime: I didn't change scheduling. Runtime logs show longer wait on hostfs reads at the tail. Example stack snippet (trimmed): 
```
get_kv_cache -> hostfs_read -> blk_mq_dispatch -> wait_for_completion
```

jess-support: Field team reported one customer with repeated 504s and they repro with a simple loop that hits the prefix cache miss pattern. Repro steps provided: 
1) POST /v1/generate with prompt that forces cache miss
2) Repeat with concurrency 20
Observed: request latencies blow up after ~30s.

emma-ml: This matches our latency distribution when prefix cache misses cause downstream NVMe reads for embeddings store. If host I/O stalls p99 will blow up even if median stays ok.

alex-sre: To triage: 1) isolate a host, run fio stressing sequential/random reads at qdepth=64 to reproduce tail; 2) check dmesg for blk warnings and blk_mq logs; 3) try setting elevator noop or sched_mq_defer_to_legacy for test.

sarah-infra: I'm on it. Spun up an isolated repro host (host-uw2-debug-02). Running: 
```
fio --name=rr --rw=randread --bs=4k --iodepth=64 --numjobs=8 --runtime=300 --time_based
```
Result: tail latencies jump dramatically when host clock sync is active; dmesg shows repeated "blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector ..." alternating with "io scheduler: throughput degraded" (snip).

deploy-bot: kernel-5.15.72 rolled out to us-west2-hostpool at 2026-03-16T22:45:02Z

mike-rt: For immediate mitigation: 1) pause kernel rollout to remaining hosts; 2) for already-upgraded hosts, pin affected pods to non-upgraded hosts or move workload; 3) temporarily lower runtime batch sizes to reduce I/O amplification.

ryan-eng-runtime: Rolling back kernel on two hot hosts now and moving traffic via smart routing to dedicated fallback pool. Also reducing batching from 16->8 for generation model X until we confirm I/O behaviour.

jess-support: Notifying impacted customers with ETA and advising graceful retry/backoff on client side.

sarah-infra: After rolling back on 2 hosts and routing away, p99 started to return toward baseline within ~6 minutes on those hosts. We still need root cause: kernel timesync changed timer tick behavior which appears to interact with hostfs/blk_mq path causing queueing.

emma-ml: Next actions: run kernel boot + fio + perf trace comparisons; try switching nvme queueing params: num_io_queues and request_mode; test NVMe firmware on repro hosts.

alex-sre: I'll open an incident ticket with kernel vendor and NVMe vendor logs attached. Also file a postmortem plan and include customer impact timeline.

sarah-infra: Thanks all. Keeping this thread updated. If you see lingering 5xxs, @jess-support escalate to SE for that customer. :eyes:

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0316-uw2-p99-io-spike (priority: high)
